","nid":"922"},{"title":"University of Michigan Seeks Postdoctoral Researcher - AI for Biomedical Data","body":"

The University of Michigan is looking for a Postdoctoral Researcher to join an interdisciplinary team advancing AI-driven research in biomedical data integration and disease modeling.

","field_thumbnail_image":"","nid":"910"},{"title":"University of Michigan Seeks Full-Time Research Assistant for AI and Diabetes Project","body":"

The Gilbert S. Omenn Department of Computational Medicine and Bioinformatics at the University of Michigan Medical School is hiring a full-time Research Assistant to join an NIH-funded project developing multimodal AI systems for Type 1 Diabetes. The position offers the chance to work with large-scale biomedical datasets and collaborate with an interdisciplinary team of scientists and clinicians.

","nid":"890"},{"title":"HIRN congratulates Enrique Eduardo Sanchez Castro as the PanKbase DEPOSIT award winner","body":"

Enrique Eduardo Sanchez Castro, a PhD candidate at Washington University in St. Louis, has been awarded the PanKbase DEPOSIT award through the HIRN Data Scholars Initiative for his project to build a harmonized, multiomic atlas of stem cell-derived islet differentiation, which will advance data accessibility and research in diabetes therapy.

","nid":"860"},{"title":"HIRN Announces Data Scholar Award: Please Welcome Dr. Matthew Ishahak to PanKbase","body":"

Dr. Matthew Ishahak, PhD, joins HIRN’s Pancreas Knowledgebase Program (PanKbase) as a Data Scholar, bringing his expertise in engineered organoids and advanced sequencing technologies. His project will use multi-omic data to unravel how diabetes disrupts gene regulatory networks in pancreatic islet cells, aiming to identify key drivers of disease progression.

","field_thumbnail_image":"

","nid":"852"},{"title":"PanKbase Team to Present Latest Advances at HIRN Annual Investigators Meeting","body":"

The Human Islet Research Network (HIRN) Annual Investigators Meeting will feature a variety of presentations, including talks from the PanKbase team, who will share their latest research and insights. The meeting offers an opportunity for investigators across the network to connect, discuss new developments, and foster collaborations in the field of islet biology and diabetes research.

","field_thumbnail_image":"

","nid":"846"},{"title":"PanKbase and DKNET Team Up to Empower Researchers with Data Mining Bootcamp","body":"

PanKbase team and DKNET hosted a bootcamp for the Sugar Science D challenge, teaching researchers how to mine datasets from PanKbase and Panc-DB.

","field_thumbnail_image":"

","nid":"843"},{"title":"Postdoctoral Position Open: AI/ML and Diabetes Research","body":"

The dkNET team at UCLA, part of the NIDDK Information Network, is inviting applications for a postdoctoral researcher with strong expertise in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML). This position offers a unique opportunity to help advance diabetes research through the development and integration of cutting-edge AI/ML methodologies.

","field_thumbnail_image":"

","nid":"841"},{"title":"A New Collaborative to Better Predict, Prevent, and Treat Type 1 Diabetes","body":"

Introducing the Multimodal AI for Type 1 Diabetes (MAI-T1D) project. Lead by PanKbase MPI, Jie Liu, the NEW multimodal AI for T1D project aims to use the latest advances in AI and health data to speed discovery of treatments for T1D. Also included in this project are PanKbase MPIs Marcela Brissova, shuibing chen, and Steve Parker. https://diabetes.med.umich.edu/events-news/news/new-collaborative-better-predict-prevent-and-treat-type-1-diabetes

","field_thumbnail_image":"

","nid":"840"},{"title":"NIDDK Grants $3.4M to Unlock Genetic & Environmental Drivers of Type 1 Diabetes","body":"

PanKbase researchers Dr. Shuibing Chen of Weill Cornell Medicine and Dr. Stephen Parker of the University of Michigan have secured a $3.4 million NIH grant to investigate the interplay of genetic risk variants and environmental triggers in how type 1 diabetes develops. Using tools like organoid models and detailed molecular profiling, the study aims to reveal what causes the immune system to attack insulin-producing beta cells, potentially facilitating early detection and intervention.
